title: Goodman Furnace Code E4: Open High-Limit Switch
meaning: The furnace overheated and the high-limit safety switch shut it down to prevent damage or fire.
diySteps: Turn off the furnace at the switch.
Check the air filter; replace if dirty (most common cause).
Open all supply vents in the house.
Restore power and see if the code clears.
whenToCallPro: If the code returns after a filter change, the blower motor or limit switch likely needs service.

title: Goodman Furnace Code E0: Ignition Failure
meaning: The furnace tried to light the burners but ignition did not occur after several attempts.
commonCauses: Closed gas valve or supply issue
Faulty flame sensor sending false readings
diySteps: Confirm the gas supply valve near the furnace is fully open.
Check that the thermostat is calling for heat.
Reset power to the furnace and observe one ignition cycle.
If the ignitor glows but burners never light, stop and call a technician.
whenToCallPro: If the ignitor glows orange but no flame appears, or if you smell gas at any point, call a licensed HVAC technician.

title: Goodman Furnace Code E1: Gas Valve Relay Error
meaning: The control board detected a problem with the gas valve circuit and locked out the furnace for safety.
commonCauses: Loose or corroded wiring at the gas valve
whenToCallPro: Gas valve and combustion issues require a licensed technician. Do not attempt to bypass safety circuits.
dangerNote: If you smell gas, leave the house and call your gas utility before anything else.

title: Goodman Furnace Code E2: Pressure Switch Failure
meaning: The pressure switch did not close when the inducer motor ran, so the furnace will not allow ignition.
diySteps: Turn off power to the furnace.
Inspect the vent pipe for obvious blockages or disconnections.
Check the condensate drain line for clogs.
Restore power and test; if the code persists, the switch or inducer may need replacement.
whenToCallPro: If the venting looks intact and the drain is clear but the code remains, a technician should test the pressure switch and inducer motor.

title: Goodman Furnace Code E3: Inducer Motor Fault
meaning: The inducer motor did not start or did not reach the speed needed to safely vent combustion gases.
diySteps: Turn off power at the furnace switch.
Listen for humming without the fan spinning — that can indicate a seized motor.
Check the exhaust vent outlet for blockages such as debris or ice.
If the motor does not spin freely by hand, do not force it — schedule service.
whenToCallPro: Inducer motors handle combustion exhaust. If the motor will not start after clearing the vent, have a technician diagnose and replace it.

title: Goodman Furnace Code E5: Flame Sensor Issue
meaning: The flame sensor did not detect a stable flame after ignition, causing the furnace to shut down.
commonCauses: Corroded or dirty flame sensor rod
diySteps: Turn off power to the furnace.
Locate the thin metal rod near the burners (the flame sensor).
Gently clean the rod with fine steel wool or emery cloth.
Reinstall, restore power, and run a heat cycle.
whenToCallPro: If cleaning the sensor does not fix the problem after two attempts, the sensor or gas valve may need professional diagnosis.
